tips.text: Wait for Harrow's Circuit week if you can stomach the delay; it skips the Defection grind.
Bring Volt or Wisp to Defection; speeding the defectors up is what keeps them alive.
Stay through all 8 squads for Rotation C; leaving at Rotation B pays about 6% instead of 15%.
Bring Oberon, Trinity, Nezha or a wide Nova if the defectors keep dying.
Bring life-support batteries and watch the route ahead of the group, where Eximus units spawn.
Do not restart a Defection run because a defector died; only cleared waves count.
Expect defectors to stick in walls or wander off; no frame fixes it, so only speed and survivability help.
Ignore Red Veil assassins in Defection; they hunt the Kavor, not you.
Run Pago solo and extract after one clean run; Rotation A means every run is a roll.
Pick a Void Fissure mission and frame that kill Corrupted enemies fast, and crack relics in the same run.
Atlas with Ore Gaze is a recommended pick for more eligible drops from Corrupted enemies.
Confirm Harrow is the offered frame in the Circuit before committing to it.
Claiming Harrow from the Circuit before Chains of Harrow skips the quest's reward path.
Farm the 2,000 Kuva before the final build; Taveuni Survival pays it while you chase Systems.
Players near-universally hate Defection; Systems took anywhere from one run to over 50 Rotation C clears.
Nobody regrets owning Harrow once the Systems grind is done.
